newsitem.title: USA: Toll Brothers sees 1997 as record year.
newsitem.headline: Toll Brothers sees 1997 as record year.

text.p: Luxury home builder Toll Brothers Inc said Wednesday it expects fiscal 1997 to be a record year for the company, given the earnings and backlog orders it has accumulated during the first half.
"With six months of record earnings, revenues and backlog already in place, we believe the prospects are excellent that fiscal 1997 will be another record year," it said.

"Increased sales per community, rising home prices and an increase in larger homes in more expensive communities pushed our backlog to a record $644 million," it said, up 15 percent from a year earlier.
The company said it was equally optimistic about the prospects for fiscal 1998.
"If the market remains stable, we believe fiscal 1998 should be an excellent year," it said.
Toll Brothers reported fully-diluted per share income of $0.35 for the second quarter ended April 30, up from $0.23 a year ago.
"This was a tremendous quarter," it said. "Standard & Poor's upgraded our corporate credit rating to investment grade and we signed more new contracts than ever before."
For the first half, earnings rose to $0.67 a share from $0.46 a year ago.
